_comment: A waiver is a declaration that stands without a passing measurement, and the reason is the
whole content of it. Only one kind belongs here: a capability with no accuracy axis to
measure. A model that measured badly does not get waived because the measurement is
inconvenient -- that is the failure this gate exists to stop, and leaving the gate red is the
correct outcome until the gap closes, the declaration is dropped, or someone accepts the gap
in writing by adding an entry here with their reason.
tiny/liveness: A liveness check's only correct answer is a few tokens saying the session is alive. There is no accuracy axis: the prompt carries no question, so no public dataset can score it and no frontier comparison means anything. Latency is the whole metric and it is measured, in evidence/fleet-routing/runs/.
